found_values.value: The F4 encoder mounted on the servo output shaft. R11 selects no position sensor of its own; the parts of the function 'encoder input' serve it. An accelerometer on the control surface is not the source: rotation about the gravity vector is not observable, so a vertical hinge line reads zero across its throw. The servo screen takes the measured position as a pulse width in µs (servo_screen_feedback(position_us, ...)), so firmware maps the encoder count to µs.

found_values.value: The one input a panel setting picks; it fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action. The panel already enables and places a rotation input by setting (Optical tacho, Tacho pin), and the BENCH page carries one rpm register with one valid bit. Hardware consequence: every rotation input keeps its own front end and GPIO, none is multiplexed, so any one can be picked. Derived from the tree; no owner figure.
found_values.source: checkout c25aa863372d: shared/settings/settings.c:99-104 (SET_OPTICAL_EN 'Optical tacho', SET_OPTICAL_PIN 'Tacho pin'); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:432, :434; shared/link/include/link_pages.h:233 (cited by P1, T1/005-P1-R11.json)

found_values.value: 65,535 rpm: the highest speed the BENCH rpm register carries; to_u16 saturates there, so an input that stops earlier truncates a reading the link could carry. Consequences: once-per-revolution inputs and the vibration fundamental reach 65,535 / 60 = 1,092 Hz; an input at the motor's electrical frequency (phase-wire clip) reaches 1,092 Hz x 21 pole pairs = 22,937 Hz (MOTOR_POLES up to 42). For comparison, a commercial stand's optical probe reads up to 30,000 rpm (Tyto Flight Stand 50 datasheet) and its electrical probe up to 190,000 eRPM (Series 1585 datasheet V2.4, Table 1). Read from the tree, not an owner figure.
found_values.source: checkout c25aa863372d: shared/bench/bench_state.c:21-28 (to_u16: scaled >= 65535 gives 65535); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:430, :487; docs/Link.md:159-160 (MOTOR_POLES even, 2 to 42); https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf (RPM up to 30,000, read 2026-09-28T15:04:45Z); https://cdn.rcbenchmark.com/landing_pages/Manuals/Series%201585%20Datasheet.pdf (Angular speed 0 to 190k eRPM, read 2026-09-28T15:04:20Z)

found_values.value: 10 rpm, read by at least one of the optical index, the magnetic pickup or the encoder. The phase-wire clip is not required to cover it: a commercial stand's electrical rpm probe 'does not work effectively when the motor is running at low RPM (<500)', while its optical probe measures 10 to 30,000 rpm. With the tree's 200 ms staleness rule for a rotation reading, a once-per-revolution input updates within 200 ms only above 300 rpm; below that firmware holds the last period.
found_values.source: https://cdn.rcbenchmark.com/landing_pages/Manuals/Series%201585%20Datasheet.pdf, Tyto Robotics Series 1585 Datasheet V2.4 2024-08-01, page 7, Optical RPM Probe; checkout c25aa863372d firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:663 (RPM_STALE_MS 200u); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:489

found_values.value: 100 V at the clip's input (the divider and clamp, round 2). The phase node swings between the IO board ground and the pack node, which R3's clamp keeps under the INA238's 85 V absolute maximum (R3's found value V34: at least 17.8 V above 67.2 V, met by a 100 V rating). The switching overshoot of a motor phase above the pack node is not found at a primary source; 100 V, the rating R3 found for parts on the same pack node, is applied and gives 15 V above the 85 V clamp ceiling.

found_values.value: Galvanically, clipped onto the bare conductor or a lug of the motor phase lead. A commercial stand measures the motor's electrical rpm and its winding resistance through its own connection to the motor wires (no-solder board, lug connectors for bullet connectors or bare wires); a winding resistance is not measurable without contact.

found_values.value: Not isolated: referenced to the IO board ground, which the ESC pack's return reaches at the star point by its own lead. The INA238 already measures the pack node against that ground, so the clip adds no new ground path and no isolator is selected.

found_values.value: A Hall-effect bipolar latch with a digital output, selected by R11, on a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles (as V221), supplied at 3.3 V from the IO board's logic rail; its open-drain output is pulled up to 3.3 V on the IO board, so it never drives an RP2354B pin above the rail and needs no level translation. A latch switches on a south pole (BOP) and releases on a north pole (BRP), which V218's two opposite magnets present once a turn.
found_values.source: DRV5015 datasheet SBAS915A, section 1 and Figure (output states: switches at BOP south, releases at BRP north), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5015.pdf; checkout c25aa863372d hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:104 (a 5 V output that can drive before the 3.3 V rail is up is translated); sourcing rule 1, hardware/docs/Research.md:134-139

found_values.value: One pulse per revolution, from two equal magnets of opposite polarity fixed 180° apart on the rotating part; the latch sees one south and one north pole a turn. Two equal masses at equal radius 180° apart add no static unbalance, which the balancing guide's rule against mass on the bell asks for. Reading the rotor's own poles instead (MOTOR_POLES / 2 pulses, up to 21) would put the latch at 22,937 Hz at 65,535 rpm, above the guaranteed bandwidth of every latch found (20 kHz minimum for DRV5013 and DRV5015, 10 kHz for TLE4961-1M). With one pulse a turn the highest rate is 1,092 Hz and the reading does not use MOTOR_POLES.
found_values.source: checkout c25aa863372d docs/Balance.md:35-36 ('Anything attached to the bell is mass on the part being balanced'); DRV5015 datasheet SBAS915A section 6.6 (fBW 20 kHz min, 30 kHz typ), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5015.pdf (2026-09-28T15:17:23Z); DRV5013 datasheet SLIS150N (fBW 20 kHz min), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5013.pdf (15:17:23Z); TLE4961-1M datasheet Rev 1.2 Table 5 (fSW 0 to 10 kHz), https://www.infineon.com/assets/row/public/documents/24/49/infineon-tle4961-1m-datasheet-en.pdf (15:19:01Z)

found_values.value: R11 selects the sensor itself: a reflective infrared sensor on a probe board of its own that JLCPCB assembles, on a lead, aimed from below at the pen line, supplied at 3.3 V from the IO board's logic rail. Its analogue output runs on the lead to a comparator with hysteresis on the IO board (the seeds TLV3201 and TLV7011 are comparators), whose push-pull output drives the GPIO. A commercial stand's optical rpm probe is likewise a small circuit board carrying the optical sensor, powered from the stand (5 V there); 3.3 V is used here so the probe is unpowered whenever the RP2354B's rail is down.
found_values.source: https://www.tytorobotics.com/blogs/series-1520-1580-1585-troubleshooting/optical-probe ('the optical sensor on the optical RPM probe circuit', 'powered by a 5V power', read 2026-09-28T15:07:50Z); checkout c25aa863372d hardware/docs/Research.md:289 (R11 seeds TLV3201, TLV7011); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:104, :441; docs/Balance.md:32-37

found_values.value: Analogue. The specification requires an analogue sensor into an ADC on the IO board and requires the accelerometer and the index pulse to be sampled on one timebase on the coprocessor. A digital accelerometer samples on its own oscillator, so its sampling instant is not on the coprocessor's timebase.
found_values.source: checkout c25aa863372d hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:447 (Vibration sensor, required), :450 (Timebase, required); docs/Manifest.md:30; docs/Balance.md:57-63

found_values.value: The frequency of each of A and B, in Hz. Encoder datasheets state the highest rate per channel: Broadcom's 'Count Frequency f = Velocity (rpm) x N/60' with N in cycles per revolution, 100 kHz; US Digital's 'Max. A/B Frequency' 300 to 720 kHz beside CPR and PPR = 4 x CPR. So 5 MHz on RS-422 is 20 million counts per second (50 ns between quadrature edges) and 1 MHz single-ended is 4 million counts per second (250 ns).
found_values.source: https://docs.broadcom.com/doc/AV02-1046EN (HEDS-55xx/56xx data sheet, Count Frequency row, read 2026-09-28T15:11:07Z); https://www.usdigital.com/media/2jklg4hq/e5-datasheet.pdf served as https://cdn.usdigital.com/assets/datasheets/datasheet-e5.pdf (E5, Max. A/B Frequency, 15:11:08Z)

found_values.value: 12 V withstand, 5 V operation. The single-ended form reads 5 V logic (F4), and the input withstands 12 V without damage, the supply the second jumper can put on the encoder: an encoder whose push-pull outputs swing to its supply, or a jumper set to 12 V with a 5 V encoder form, then puts up to 12 V on the signal pins.
found_values.source: checkout c25aa863372d hardware/docs/Research.md:532 (F4 answer: 5 V single-ended; supply 5 V or 12 V by a jumper); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:445

found_values.value: 8 to 288 kHz, wider than the programmer screen's 24, 48 and 96 kHz. AM32 accepts a PWM frequency setting from 8 to 144 kHz (pwm_frequency < 145 && > 7), and its variable-PWM mode 1 lowers the auto-reload to half, up to twice the setting. The 24/48/96 kHz list is BLHeli_S's (shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:115). The clip's front end must pass up to 22,937 Hz (V212 x 21 pole pairs): that overlaps an 8 kHz PWM, so no fixed low-pass separates the two at every setting; against the 24 kHz lower end the margin is 1.05 x.
found_values.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/am32-firmware/AM32/main/Src/main.c lines 637-644 and 1977-1980 (read 2026-09-28T15:06:14Z); checkout c25aa863372d shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:115

report.value: One RP2354B PIO state machine running the pico-examples quadrature_encoder program; no external decoder. The program samples A and B in a loop of at most 10 cycles and reads step rates up to sysclk / 10: 15 Msteps/s at the RP2350's 150 MHz maximum system clock. That covers the single-ended form (1 MHz a channel, 4 Mcounts/s) and RS-422 up to 3.75 MHz a channel, not the 5 MHz of F4 (20 Mcounts/s, V227). No quadrature decoder from an allowlisted maker was found (LS7366R and LS7184 are LSI/CSI). A PWM slice counts one edge type on its B pin only, so it gives no direction. The index pulse is captured on a GPIO edge interrupt, or counted by a PWM slice's B pin.
report.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/pico-examples/master/pio/quadrature_encoder/quadrature_encoder.pio (read 2026-09-28T15:10:24Z); RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, clock table (clk_sys 150 MHz) and section 12.5.2.5, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf served from pip-assets.raspberrypi.com (15:10:48Z); V227; jlcparts copy 2026-09-14

report.value: 1 state machine; 24 of its block's 32 instruction words, loaded at offset 0 ('.origin 0', computed jumps), leaving 8 words: no bidirectional DShot port (16 words) fits in that block beside it. 0 DMA channels: the count is pushed to the RX FIFO without blocking and read on demand. A and B on 2 consecutive GPIO (IN PINS, 2) inside the block's 32-GPIO window; the index on 1 more GPIO; 0 PWM slices, or 1 if the index is counted by a slice's B pin
report.source: quadrature_encoder.pio as above (instruction count: 14 table jumps, 1 decrement, 9 loop instructions); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:105 (PIO reach)

report.value: 6 GPIO: encoder A, B (consecutive), I; optical index; magnetic pickup; phase-wire clip. Accelerometer: 1 ADC input per axis wired (1, or 2 if R10's V201 wires both in-plane axes) if Q4 takes the RP2354B's ADC; otherwise the external converter's interface (R10)

The clip must pass the motor's electrical frequency up to 22,937 Hz (65,535 rpm x 21 pole pairs) and reject ESC PWM from 8 kHz (AM32) to 288 kHz. The bands overlap below 22.9 kHz, so no fixed low-pass meets both at every setting; against the tree's 24/48/96 kHz list the margin is 1.05 x. The clip's front end needs a method that does not rest on frequency separation alone, or the owner narrows V212 or V229 for this input

1,092 Hz at 65,535 rpm with V218's one pulse a turn. Reading the rotor's own poles (up to 21 pairs) needs 22,937 Hz, above every latch found: DRV5015 and DRV5013 guarantee 20 kHz (30 kHz typical), TLE4961-1M 10 kHz, A1220 states none

ADXL316 and ADXL326 outputs leave through an internal filter resistor of 32 kΩ (27 to 37 kΩ on the ADXL316) that sets the bandwidth with CX, CY; the lead's capacitance and the converter's sampling input load it, and the resistor's tolerance and drift shift the phase at 1,092 Hz. R10 and round 2 decide whether the sensor board carries a buffer. The ADXL1002 seed, a buffered output part, has no JLCPCB stock (0, presale −1)
report.source: ADXL316 datasheet Rev. C Table 1 note 5 (15:16:01Z); ADXL326 Rev. 0 Table 1 note 5 (15:16:00Z); vendors.py jlcpcb C662288 (15:14:54Z)
